title: Google's November Pixel Drop Brings Gemini Intelligence to the Pixel 10
excerpt: Rambler, multi-step task automation and proactive suggestions reach last year's flagships, alongside a $29.99 Pixel Tag tracker and a smarter Call Screen for the Pixel 11.
body:
• Google's November Pixel Drop, rolling out from November 10 over several weeks, brings Gemini Intelligence to the Pixel 10, 10 Pro, 10 Pro XL and 10 Pro Fold.
  • Pixel 10 owners get Rambler voice typing, Gemini multi-step task automation and proactive suggestions; several features are limited to select regions and languages, and Gemini calling is US-only.
  • Google also launched Pixel Tag, a tracker priced at $29.99 for one or $99.99 for a four-pack, available November 11 with a battery rated for over a year.
  • Pixel 11 phones get a more conversational Gemini Call Screen, and conversation summaries expand to Hindi and five other languages.

Google's November Pixel Drop is the update that closes the gap between its current phones and last year's. The headline change, announced in Google's Pixel Drop post, is Gemini Intelligence arriving on the Pixel 10 series: the Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10 Pro XL and Pixel 10 Pro Fold gain features that debuted on the Pixel 11, including Rambler, personalised suggestions and multi-step task automation. Updates started rolling out on November 10 and will continue over the next several weeks.

What Pixel 10 owners actually get

Rambler is the voice-typing upgrade: it removes filler words such as "um" and formats spoken thoughts into polished text before you send. Android Authority reported Rambler is the exception to the Drop's regional limits, available in all regions and languages, while most other Gemini Intelligence features are restricted to select regions and languages.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=rUqLlMVJE3w

Gemini can now complete multi-step tasks on the Pixel 10 — ordering groceries, booking a ride, ordering takeout or finding a restaurant reservation — with availability for that automation now covering Japan, the UK and India, according to Google. Proactive Gemini Actions can summarise selected text from the contextual menu and send grocery items mentioned in a conversation straight to a Google Keep list. The Pixel 10 series also gets Create My Widget, which builds personalised widgets such as a spending tracker or a trip countdown that pulls in flight and reservation details, and Extreme Charging Mode, which pauses background activity to charge faster; the Pixel 10a is excluded from the Gemini Intelligence set.

Google is also expanding the experiment that lets Gemini make routine phone calls on your behalf, using your own number in the United States to change a reservation, check inventory or ask a store to hold an item. Android Authority's rundown of the Drop counts more than a dozen features across phones, tablets and watches.

Pixel 11, watches and a new tracker

On the Pixel 11 series, Call Screen gets the upgrade: when you screen an unknown number, Gemini now asks the caller why they are reaching out in a more conversational exchange, with a live transcript on screen until you join or end the call. Conversation summaries now work in German, French, Spanish, Italian, Hindi and Traditional Chinese, and Pixel Search is available on Pixel 6 and newer devices. Pixel Watch owners get automatic unlocking when their nearby phone is unlocked, arriving in the next few weeks, and step-by-step workouts are rolling out to Pixel Watch 3 and newer.

The one new piece of hardware is Pixel Tag, Google's item tracker. It is slim enough for a wallet, runs for over a year on its battery, and uses the Find Hub network of more than one billion Android devices to locate belongings, with UWB providing direction and distance guidance when the item is nearby. Pixel Tag is available starting November 11 at $29.99 for a single tag or $99.99 for a four-pack.

What to do if you own a Pixel

Nothing is required beyond waiting for the staged rollout and checking for the update on your device over the coming weeks. The features worth enabling first are Rambler, which works everywhere, and, for US owners, Gemini's call-making, which is in public beta. Readers in India get the multi-step task automation in this Drop, one of the three regions Google named for it.
